questions.prompt: Explain how a NetTrello PATCH tells "omitted" apart from "set to null", and why that distinction matters.

keyPoints.text: Omitting description keeps the old one; sending null clears it.
keyPoints.quote: An omitted description means preserve the old description. A JSON `null` description means clear it.

keyPoints.text: A non-nullable JsonElement has three states: Undefined, Null, and a value.
keyPoints.quote: Nonnullable `JsonElement` observes three states: `Undefined` for omission, `Null` for clearing, and a value kind for replacement.

keyPoints.text: Making it JsonElement? collapses JSON null into CLR null and loses the distinction.
keyPoints.quote: Nullable `JsonElement?` loses that distinction during deserialization because JSON null becomes CLR null.

keyPoints.text: Unknown properties are rejected by the serializer instead of being silently ignored.
keyPoints.quote: so `{"titel":"typo"}` is a 400 rather than a silently ignored no-op.

keyPoints.text: Omission cannot bypass the required-title rule because the existing title is carried forward.
keyPoints.quote: a caller cannot use omission to bypass a required title rule: the existing title is carried forward and remains valid.

keyPoints.text: Confusing the two turns a rename into silent data loss.
keyPoints.quote: getting that distinction wrong turns a rename into silent data loss.

questions.prompt: Walk through validate-before-mutate for card updates and moves: what is checked, in what order, and what the repository clone does and does not protect.

keyPoints.text: A card update computes title, description and labels into locals first.
keyPoints.quote: A card update first computes required title, optional description, and normalized labels in local variables.

keyPoints.text: So a late invalid label leaves every property unassigned.
keyPoints.quote: If a late label is empty or too long, no property has been assigned.

keyPoints.text: A full target column is refused before the source card is removed.
keyPoints.quote: A full target is rejected before the source card is removed.

keyPoints.text: A same-column reorder is a separate operation because it does not add a card to the column.
keyPoints.quote: Same-column reorder is a distinct operation because moving a card within a full column does not increase cardinality.

keyPoints.text: The callback works on a clone, so a failed move leaves the stored board unchanged.
keyPoints.quote: A failed move therefore leaves the stored board unchanged even when the callback had begun work on its clone.

keyPoints.text: The clone does not excuse mutate-first domain code: callers can still see a corrupted clone.
keyPoints.quote: callers can still observe a corrupted in-memory clone, timestamps can change, and later callback logic can make a wrong decision.

questions.prompt: Explain the board version as a concurrency precondition, and how the in-memory guarantees translate to a real database.

keyPoints.text: The version is an aggregate-level precondition, not a per-field merge.
keyPoints.quote: The version value is an aggregate-level precondition, not a field-level merge.

keyPoints.text: The check runs while the semaphore is held, so decision and replacement are serialized.
keyPoints.quote: The in-memory repository checks the value while its semaphore is held, so the conflict decision and replacement are serialized.

keyPoints.text: A disabled button is not enough: the service must reject an old header itself.
keyPoints.quote: a caller can still send an old header, and the service remains responsible for rejecting it.

keyPoints.text: A semaphore guards one process; a concurrency token guards every process.
keyPoints.quote: A semaphore protects one process; a token protects every process on every machine.

keyPoints.text: Clone-on-read becomes AsNoTracking for reads you will not save.
keyPoints.quote: `AsNoTracking()` for reads you will not save.

keyPoints.text: The card-limit count and the insert must share a transaction or two concurrent adds both pass.
keyPoints.quote: the count and the insert must be in one transaction, or two concurrent adds both pass the check.
